item: fts_status takes rows from a covering-index count of articles (count(1), which the deadline can stop) instead of a scan of the full-text table: 30 times cheaper cold at 1,000,000 articles; the premise that a count of articles is a corpus scan is withdrawn
summary: Follow-on to #1534, from the WAL lane's cold encrypted measurement at 1,000,000 articles (R295). Step 3 of fts_status read SELECT count(*) FROM article_fts; for an external-content FTS5 table that reads every row of the content table, so it cost a table scan of articles (9.6 to 11.9 s cold, 5.5 to 6.0 s warm, 99% of the call, 3 to 5 s from its own 15 s deadline, and it follows the article TEXT, so a real store would time out at far fewer articles) to give the number that a count over a covering index gives in 0.24 to 0.33 s cold. NOW: rows is SELECT count(1) FROM articles inside the same count deadline; count_status, the probe, #1534's one-statement ends and population and every key and label are unchanged. It is count(1) and not count(*) because SQLite runs a bare count(*) as ONE opcode that the deadline's progress handler is never consulted during (found by the independent read of this PR and reproduced: 0 consultations against 30 to 450 for count(1) over the same covering index, and a 0.5 s deadline around count(*) over 6,000,000 rows returned after 0.74 s with no StatementTimeout), so only count(1) keeps count_status timed_out reachable. fts_status whole, cold, 5 runs on an encrypted 1,000,000-article store: 294 / 373 / 488 ms (min / median / max) against 9,729 / 11,382 / 11,975 (30 times less at the median); warm 17 / 24 / 26 against 5,539 / 5,801 / 6,009 (the row loop costs 16 to 24 ms warm where count(*) costs 1); corpus_integrity cold 11.7 / 14.6 / 15.3 s against 17.2 / 17.3 / 17.4 (the rest is PRAGMA foreign_key_check, 10.9 to 14.6 s, untouched). The docstrings of ensure_fts and fts_status no longer say a count of articles is a corpus scan (the 74 s cold figure on a 2.7 GB corpus was not reproduced on the current schema); the boot still compares no counts, left as a decision. Tests: the seven that simulated the old statement or pinned 'no statement counts the articles' are rewritten, not deleted; new: rows equals the old statement over a full / shrunken / emptied / partial index, a partial index still reads partial (inferred) with the count answered and timed out, the deadline's value is pinned (at both call sites and in the function itself), and the real deadline, at a millionth of a second over 30,000 articles, must stop the count (a count(*) respelling returns whole and fails it). Mutants: 8 of 8 red on the first version, 7 of 7 on the first fold, 7 of 7 more on the second, and the 2 the independent read's 22 left alive (the deadline's value) are red. LIMITS: one machine and a 1.3 GB/s virtual disk, synthetic Latin text of 1.3 KB per article, nothing above 1 M; the covering index is the planner's pick (idx_article_created_at on the measured store, about 4 times the pages of the smallest candidate); 'same number' holds on a store whose indexes agree with their table, and the new count no longer reads article pages, so a damaged articles page no longer surfaces in this block; step 4's shadow-table count(*) and integrity.py's own count(*) are uninterruptible simple counts bounded by table size (61 to 82 ms cold at 1 M for the shadow table), unchanged.
